title: Object-Oriented Design Principles
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of object-oriented design principles using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates object-oriented design principles.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Object-Oriented Design Principles** as part of **Inheritance, Interfaces, and Polymorphism**. Classes group state and behavior; primary constructors and properties keep ordinary domain models concise, while initialization order still matters. Use the subtopics—Single Responsibility, Open/Closed and Dependency Inversion, Favoring Composition Where Appropriate—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

items.title: Single Responsibility
items.text: Single Responsibility is one part of object-oriented design principles. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.text: Open/Closed and Dependency Inversion means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Save the snippet in a Kotlin/JVM console project and run the configured Gradle application task, or use the Kotlin Playground for examples that need no external dependencies.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the documented starting values, rerun the smallest test, and compare the result with the expected output. If behavior differs, check the compiler/plugin/runtime versions and the active target before changing more than one thing.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: Object-Oriented Design Principles removes the need to test boundary conditions or verify the chosen runtime/library version.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small variation that demonstrates object-oriented design principles. Write down your predicted result first, run it in the correct local project, then explain one boundary case involving single responsibility.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain object-oriented design principles without copying the lesson wording.
